sentences.text: Xenoceratops is distinguished from other ceratopsids by unique details of the bony ornamentation on its frill.
It is apomorphic for having ovoid depressions with arched ventral margins where epiparietals contact and fuse, a trait not seen in other centrosaurines.
The animal lacks the P1 process, a trait shared with other basal centrosaurines like Albertaceratops and Diabloceratops.
Evidence suggests Xenoceratops had elongated, robust postorbital horns similar to those of other primitive, age-similar centrosaurines like Albertaceratops and Diabloceratops.

The right P3 process is similar to all centrosaurines except some Centrosaurus specimens, but differs from all others except Albertaceratops and Medusaceratops by being broad-based and pachyostotic, and differs from those two by being straight.
Xenoceratops shares with Albertaceratops and many casmosaurines the lack of bumps on the medial parietal ramus, and unlike other centrosaurines, lacks imbricated epiparietals on the lateral ramus.
Xenoceratops is the oldest known Canadian ceratopsid, approximately half a million years older than Albertaceratops from the lower Oldman Formation.
It is one of the oldest ceratopsids, about one million years younger than Diabloceratops from Utah.
Xenoceratops was described as a new genus and species in 2012 by Ryan, Evans, and Shepherd.
At the time of its description, Xenoceratops foremostensis was the oldest known ceratopsid taxon in Canada.
The name Xenoceratops combines Greek xenos (foreign/alien) and ceratops (horned face), referencing the lack of known ceratopsians from its formation.
The species name foremostensis refers to the town of Foremost in Alberta.
The name Xenoceratops comes from the Greek words xenos, meaning "foreign" or "strange", and ceratops, meaning "horned face".
Xenoceratops foremostensis is the type species of the genus Xenoceratops.
Xenoceratops is classified as a basal centrosaurine.
Descriptores classified Xenoceratops in Centrosaurinae in a basal position.
Xenoceratops belongs to the parent group Centrosaurinae.
Xenoceratops is a member of the family Ceratopsidae.
Xenoceratops is classified in the class Ornithischia.
Xenoceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous (middle Campanian stage) in what is now Alberta, Canada.
Xenoceratops lived 79 million years ago during the middle Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
Xenoceratops lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
